title: The shell actually is the shell
description: Every page's <main> currently shrink-wraps its content instead of filling the max-w-6xl shell, and /templates blows the document out to 10384px at a 1440px viewport. Both are the same family of bug: a container whose width is decided by its content. Fix (proven at runtime in the browser before being written): drop `flex flex-col` from <body> in layout.tsx — an auto margin on the cross axis disables flex stretch, which is why mx-auto never worked — and add min-w-0 to the grid children in TemplateManager.tsx:170 and Studio.tsx:160, because a `1fr` track's implicit min-width:auto resolves to min-content and grows past any overflow-x-auto on a descendant. Nothing uses the body flex; there is no sticky footer.
acceptanceCriteria: At 1440px, main.x == 144 and main.width == 1152 on /, /studio, /posts, /templates, /assets, /scoreboard
/posts/[id] stays at 336/768 — max-w-3xl is a deliberate reading measure, do not widen it
document.scrollWidth == 1440 on all seven routes at a 1440px viewport
/posts and /scoreboard no longer exceed 390px scrollWidth at a 390px viewport; wide tables scroll inside their own container
Measurements come from getBoundingClientRect in a real browser, recorded in progress.txt — not inferred from classnames
slice tests green

title: Dates carry their year
description: Explorer.tsx:77 formats dates as {day, month} with no year, on a corpus spanning 2024-01-25 to 2026-07-17. The engagement chart's axis reads 26 Jan / 27 Feb / 14 Mar / 17 Sept / 01 Apr and looks unsorted. It is not — series at :200 sorts ascending by published_at. The label is what lies. The table's Published column has the same formatter and is worse, because the table sorts by engagement so two rows both reading '15 Jun' can be two years apart.
acceptanceCriteria: Chart axis and table Published column both disambiguate the year across a multi-year corpus
A test pins that two posts on the same day-and-month in different years render differently
The existing ascending published_at sort in `series` is untouched — it was always correct
slice tests green

title: Form controls join the design system
description: US-004 in the V2 run recorded 'the Select migration is US-004's' and it never happened. /studio renders three raw <select> elements, /posts four more plus a bare dd/mm/yyyy date input, /templates one, and /assets an unstyled native file input. They carry OS chrome next to tokenised Buttons and are the loudest visual inconsistency in the app. Radix Select is already vendored. Note the known trap: Radix Select cannot hold an empty-string value, so 'all' options need a sentinel, and if that sentinel reaches the query string filtering breaks silently while everything still renders.
acceptanceCriteria: No raw <select> remains on /studio, /posts, /templates
The 'all'/'let it suggest' sentinel never reaches the query string — a test asserts the built query for the default filter state
Keyboard: the control opens, arrow-keys and Escape work; assert our own logic, not Radix's internals
The native file input on /assets is styled or replaced without losing drag-and-drop
slice tests green

title: The three scoreboard tables share one column grid
description: Status lands at x=646 under HOOK, x=666 under STRUCTURE and x=504 under VISUAL, with Posts/Engaged/Mean/Evidence shifting behind it. Three tables of identical shape that read as unrelated because each sizes its own columns to its own content.
acceptanceCriteria: The three tables' column edges align; verified by measurement in a browser, not by eye
No aggregate loses its sample count and no 'not ranked' copy is removed — those are load-bearing
slice tests green

title: An image bomb is refused, not a 500
description: assets.py:114 catches (OSError, ValueError). PIL's DecompressionBombError subclasses Exception directly, so a 68-byte PNG declaring 30000x30000 escapes the handler and returns 500 where the docstring promises a 4xx. Verified empirically during the V2 review.
acceptanceCriteria: A 68-byte PNG declaring 30000x30000 returns 422 with a message naming the reason
Nothing is written to disk for a rejected upload
The existing UnreadableUpload path for truncated/corrupt files still returns 422
slice tests green

title: A verdict can be cleared, not only changed
description: PRD.md:178 said {verdict: null} clears a ruling; main.py:272 makes VerdictIn.verdict required, so it cannot. Do NOT widen it to a bare `Verdict | None` — that makes the field optional-with-default, so an empty body or a mistyped key would silently wipe a ruling instead of returning 422. Use an explicit clear path: either DELETE /posts/{id}/verdict, or required-but-nullable via Field(...).
acceptanceCriteria: Clearing a verdict nulls verdict_at, empties verdict_note, and returns the post to Inbox queue 4
An empty request body is still a 422, not an accidental clear — this is the whole point of the slice
An unknown verdict string is still a 422 naming the three allowed values
slice tests green
A ruling can be retracted from /posts/[id] — the API-only version is the exact shape that blocked the V2 merge (a verdict route with no form)

title: The system-status row can report a failure
description: (inbox)/page.tsx:196 renders the API row inside the `health.ok` branch with ok={health.ok}, so it is structurally incapable of rendering anything but green. A status readout that can only say 'fine' is worse than none.
acceptanceCriteria: The API row reflects health.data.status and can render not-ok
A test drives the not-ok path and asserts it renders as a failure
The existing failure sentence for an unreachable backend is unchanged — it is deliberately not ApiFailureNotice

title: Closed circuits: N
description: PRD.md:209 marked this Build and it was silently dropped. N = drafts with went_live_at set whose post carries a verdict — one full lap of generate -> push -> publish -> rule. It reads 0 today, and showing that 0 is the entire point: the Inbox currently gives no way to know the loop has never run.

It reads 0 against today's database and the copy makes 0 legible as 'never', not as an error
Setting a verdict on a post with draft lineage moves it to 1 — asserted in a test
Naive/aware datetime comparison goes through main._utc; every datetime column is timestamp without time zone and mixing the two raises

title: Post detail shows its engagement curve and what generated it
description: GET /posts/{id}/history and draft_for_post both exist, are tested, and are called by nothing. PRD.md:186 promised both on the post page. Add the curve and the 'generated from hook X v2 / structure Y v1 / visual Z v2' lineage block. IMPORTANT: this slice adds content only — /posts/[id]'s un-tokenised styling stays deferred, and the browser pass confirmed it has no dark-mode or legibility failure. Do not opportunistically restyle the page.
acceptanceCriteria: A published post with draft lineage renders its engagement curve and its three template versions
A post with no draft behind it renders neither, and says so rather than showing an empty chart
Lineage reads the draft's own (family, version) via generated_from — never the newest version, which was G2 finding #3
No styling changes outside the two new blocks

title: Lessons reach the step that decides what to write about

acceptanceCriteria: propose_topics' prompt carries the verdict lessons; asserted against the built prompt
With no verdicts recorded the prompt is unchanged from today's — no empty 'Lessons:' header

title: A paid run says what it cost
description: There is no spend counter anywhere in this app. POST /drafts/autonomous-run clamps its cap hard (that was fixed at G2) but reports nothing about what it spent. Required before US-013 lands, because variants multiply paid calls. Separately: leave enable_autonomous alone — scheduler.py:76 is its only reader, three existing tests call this endpoint with the flag off, and gating a deliberate human click behind a scheduler switch is the wrong control. Record that decision in a comment so it stops reading as an open trap.
acceptanceCriteria: The run response reports llm_calls and image_calls actually made
The counts are observed, not predicted from the cap — a run that fails partway reports what it spent before failing
A comment at the endpoint records why enable_autonomous does not gate it
No test makes a live network call; Azure and Zernio stay behind their fakes

title: Studio can open a draft that already exists
description: The spine of phase 2 and on no previous list. Six drafts sit in the database, GET /drafts and GET /drafts/{id} both exist and are called by nothing, and Inbox queues 2 and 3 (4 built, 2 pushed) link to a bare /studio that is empty on every single visit. The Inbox points at a door that does not open. Add a drafts list and /studio?draft=<id> that loads text, visual, lineage and the existing rewrite/redraw/push actions.
acceptanceCriteria: /studio?draft=<id> loads that draft and its lineage; an unknown id says so rather than rendering the empty state
Inbox queues 2 and 3 link to the specific draft, not to bare /studio
All 6 existing drafts are reachable from the UI
Pushing from a loaded draft still creates a Zernio DRAFT and never publishes

title: One idea, several drafts, keep one
description: Generate N drafts of the same idea across different approved hook/structure/visual combinations, show them side by side, keep one and discard the rest. This is the honest form of template comparison while the corpus cannot support ranking: a human choosing between three concrete drafts is judgement, not statistics. Nothing here may rank or score the variants.
acceptanceCriteria: N is clamped server-side to a new settings.variants_max using the min(requested, ceiling) pattern at api_drafts.py:279 — a large N must be impossible, for the same reason ?cap=500 was
The clamp is a bound, not a default: a test asserts an over-large request produces at most variants_max
The response reports llm_calls and image_calls for the whole batch (US-011)
Discarded variants are deleted, not left as orphan drafts polluting Inbox queue 2
No variant is ranked, scored, or ordered by anything but generation order
slice tests green

title: Re-topic: same templates, new subject
description: Nikhil's original pillar, verbatim: 'have the template and hooks and visuals as kind of template so that we can easily recreate them using another topic.' Take any past post or existing draft and generate a NEW draft on a new idea that inherits its exact template versions. generated_from already resolves a draft's own (family, version) — this creates a new row that inherits them, rather than a rewrite that moves lineage.
acceptanceCriteria: The new draft's hook/structure/visual family+version equal the source's, resolved via generated_from and not by latest version
The source draft or post is unmodified — its lineage, text and metrics do not move
Re-topicking from a retired template version still works: the version history is the attribution record
slice tests green
UI: a re-topic can be started from a draft or a post (backend landed 33f8102)

title: Asset picker is a grid, not a select per slot

Changing the visual resets the picker to the new template's defaults
Arrow-key navigable and Escape-dismissable

title: A real route for the draft behind a post, and a nameable cost
description: posts/[id]/page.tsx:148 fetches /drafts?limit=500 and joins in the browser. The list is created_at DESC, so what falls off the end is the OLDEST drafts - exactly the ones whose posts have been live longest - and the page then says 'no draft behind this post' while the draft sits in the database. metrics.draft_for_post already does this join and has no HTTP surface. Separately, Studio's variants button cannot say what it will spend because nothing tells the client settings.variants_max; a count control would hardcode 3 and drift.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /posts/{id}/draft returns the draft for a generated post
404 for an unknown post id; 'no draft behind it' is a distinct answer from 'no such post' - most posts here have no draft
variants_max is readable by the client without exposing anything else; /health stays boolean-and-scalar and never reveals a credential value
slice tests green

title: Test integrity - hunt what is green and proves nothing
description: Three times this run a green suite proved nothing: make check never ran the frontend suite, two Studio assertions queried a detached DocumentFragment, and a surviving mutation revealed chooseVisual had zero coverage because Suggest held a duplicate copy of its two lines. Fourteen loading.tsx/error.tsx twins exist and only route-error.test.tsx covers any of it.
acceptanceCriteria: every suspect assertion is proven by MUTATING THE SOURCE and confirming the test fails - reading it is not proof
a test that survives its mutation is rewritten or deleted, and the deletion is reported
loading and error states are covered; a skeleton at a different width than its page is a visible layout jump
full suite green

title: Browser pass over the whole app, then close the version
description: Nothing has re-walked all seven routes since 15 slices stacked up; each slice verified only its own. This is the check that found both structural defects. Includes the two surfaces never yet seen rendered: the verdict retract control and 'use the template's default'.
acceptanceCriteria: 7 routes x 2 themes x 1440 and 390, findings recorded with evidence
the two never-rendered surfaces are seen, via the read-only proxy technique - NOT by writing a specimen row to the database
findings that clear the bar become slices BEFORE merge, not after
full suite green, merged to main, vault note and memory rewritten
